title: How to Set Up a Simple Bookkeeping System for Your Freelance Business
summary:
How to Set Up a Simple Bookkeeping System for Your Freelance Business

Most freelancers don't have a bookkeeping problem. They have a "where did the money go" problem — income lands in one account, expenses leak out of another, and by tax time the whole year is a pile of bank statements and guesswork.

A bookkeeping system doesn't need to be complicated. It needs to answer three questions at any moment: how much came in, how much went out, and how much is actually mine to spend. Here is the setup I use, built in one afternoon and maintained in about 30 minutes a week in the sample below.

1. Give every dollar a bucket the moment it arrives

Freelance income is not salary. No one withholds tax, no one sets aside savings, and the number that hits your account is not the number you can spend. So the first rule: split income the day it arrives, before you spend any of it.

title: How to Split Vocals and Instrumentals in Your Browser
summary:
If you want a karaoke track, a clean vocal for practice, or a stem you can slowly transcribe by ear, you do not always need a desktop DAW or a downloaded model. A browser-based AI vocal remover can separate a song into a vocal stem and an accompaniment stem on a phone or a laptop, without installing an app.

This is a practical guide to when that workflow is good enough, how to judge the result, and how to avoid the usual disappointments.

What you are actually asking the tool to do

Stem separation is not "deleting the singer from the mix" in the way a graphic designer would delete a layer. In a finished stereo file, the vocal is already baked into the same two channels as the drums, bass, and reverb. An AI vocal remover estimates which parts of the signal are likely to be a voice and which parts are likely to be the rest of the arrangement, then writes two new files.

title: aws-emulator
summary:
aws-emulator

Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so.

It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog.

It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms.

title: Send duplicates at the same time
summary:
Replaying a webhook twice in sequence can miss the race that breaks fulfillment.

Deliver the same event concurrently in a test environment. Both handlers might check "already processed?" before either saves the answer. Now both grant credits.

Use an atomic claim, such as a database uniqueness constraint, and commit the local business change consistently with the processing record. External actions need their own protection against repeats.

Test out-of-order events separately. An event ID identifies a delivery; it doesn't tell you which subscription state is current.
